stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $A$ be a ring such that every faithfully flat \'etale ring map
$A \to B$ has a retraction. Then the same is true for every quotient ring
$A/I$.
hypotheses:
Let $A$ be a ring such that every faithfully flat \'etale ring map
$A \to B$ has a retraction.
conclusions:
the same is true for every quotient ring
$A/I$.

reason: An étale faithfully flat quotient algebra A/I→Bbar lifts to an étale A-algebra B. A finite family of principal opens D(f_i) with f_i∈I covers the complement of the image of Spec B, and B×∏A_fi becomes faithfully flat étale over A while reducing to Bbar modulo I. Its retraction induces a retraction of Bbar.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $A$ be a ring such that every faithfully flat \'etale ring map
$A \to B$ has a retraction. Then every local ring of $A$ at a maximal
ideal is strictly henselian.
hypotheses:
Let $A$ be a ring such that every faithfully flat \'etale ring map
$A \to B$ has a retraction.
conclusions:
every local ring of $A$ at a maximal
ideal is strictly henselian.

reason: Given an étale neighbourhood at a maximal ideal, isolate its chosen prime in a quasi-finite fibre, extend its image to a faithfully flat étale cover using a principal open, and use the assumed retraction. Flat local maps in both directions then identify the local rings, establishing strict henselianity by the cited characterization.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A **w-local** spectral space has closed set of closed points and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a w-local map between such spaces is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. A ring map is **ind-étale** when its target is a filtered colimit of étale algebras over the source.

Let $A \to B$ be a ring map inducing algebraic extensions on residue fields.
There exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
B \ar[r] & D \\
A \ar[r] \ar[u] & C \ar[u]
}
$$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to C$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $B \to D$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $\Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D) \to \Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ is the inverse image
of the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$ surjects onto $\Spec(A)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ surjects onto $\Spec(B)$,
\item for $\mathfrak m \subset C$ maximal the local ring
$C_\mathfrak m$ is strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: A\to B induces algebraic extensions of residue fields.
conclusions:
Let $A \to B$ be a ring map inducing algebraic extensions on residue fields.
There exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
B \ar[r] & D \\
A \ar[r] \ar[u] & C \ar[u]
}
$$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to C$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $B \to D$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $\Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D) \to \Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ is the inverse image
of the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$ surjects onto $\Spec(A)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ surjects onto $\Spec(B)$,
\item for $\mathfrak m \subset C$ maximal the local ring
$C_\mathfrak m$ is strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}

reason: First constructs a faithfully flat w-local étale refinement C of A with strictly henselian local rings using earlier constructions and localization along closed points. Then applies the residue-field-extension w-localization to B⊗_A C to obtain D and verifies all nine properties via the cited lemmas.
